citations.quote: This piece is the semi-finished doucai, which only finished the underglaze blue outline and blue shades; however, the overglaze enamel parts have not yet been applied.
The best pieces of this period are characterised by light and perfectly formed bodies, delicate and controlled cobalt painting, and clear, even glazes.
Finely potted porcelain dish with gently curved, shallow sides, short foot and recessed base with a six character inscription 'Da Qing Yongzheng nian zhi' inside a double roundel.

/record/summaryDescription	The Yongzheng period (1723-1735) represents a high point in the production of blue and white porcelain at Jingdezhen. The best pieces of this period are characterised by light and perfectly formed bodies, delicate and controlled cobalt painting, and clear, even glazes. This shallow dish exhibits beautifully executed underglaze painting, using two delicate shades of monochrome blue to create perfectly controlled lines and contours. It is most likely to have been used to serve food.
/record/physicalDescription	Finely potted porcelain dish with gently curved, shallow sides, short foot and recessed base with a six character inscription 'Da Qing Yongzheng nian zhi' inside a double roundel. The outside is decorated with flowers and stylised scrolls. The inside is decorated with a central 'Shou' character surrounded by bunches of flowers, all encircled by scroll work. This piece is the semi-finished doucai, which only finished the underglaze blue outline and blue shades; however, the overglaze enamel parts have not yet been applied. The complete pieces with the same design in the Yongzheng period were auctioned on 8 October 2013 and at Christie's on 14 May 2010.
